name: Chicken Soup
ingredients:
For 2–3 portions:
2 bone-in chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or similar)
1–2 carrots, sliced
½–1 onion
1–2 garlic cloves
1–1.2 L water
Salt
Pepper
1 bay leaf
Optional: 1 small potato, chopped;  a handful of noodles or rice; parsley; 1 tbsp oil or a small piece of butter
instructions:
Put the chicken pieces in a pot and pour in 1–1.2 L water, enough to comfortably cover them. Add the onion, garlic, bay leaf, salt and pepper.
Bring the water to a boil. Once boiling, lower the heat and let the soup gently simmer for 25–30 minutes. If foam appears on top, you can remove it with a spoon.
Add the sliced carrots and chopped potato if using. Continue simmering for another 15 minutes, until the vegetables are soft.
If using noodles, add them during the last 5–7 minutes. If using rice, add it about 10 minutes before the soup is finished.
Taste the broth and add more salt or pepper if needed. Remove the onion and bay leaf if you don't want them in the finished soup.
Optional: take the chicken pieces out, remove the meat from the bones, shred it and return the meat to the soup. Finish with parsley or a small piece of butter if desired.

name: Oven-Baked Chicken Thigh & Rice
ingredients:
For 1 portion:
1 bone-in chicken thigh
½ cup rice (about 90–100 g)
1 cup hot water or broth
1 tbsp oil or a small piece of butter
Salt
Pepper
½ tsp paprika
Garlic powder or 1 garlic clove
Optional: small carrot pieces; frozen peas; sliced onion
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Add the uncooked rice to a small glass baking dish. Season it with salt, pepper, paprika and garlic. Add any vegetables you are using.
Pour in 1 cup of hot water or broth and stir once so the rice is spread evenly across the bottom of the dish.
Season the chicken thigh on both sides with salt, pepper and paprika. Rub it with a little oil and place it on top of the rice, skin-side up if it has skin.
Cover the baking dish tightly with foil or a glass lid. Bake at 190°C for 30 minutes.
Remove the cover and bake for another 15–20 minutes, until the chicken is golden and the rice is soft and has absorbed the liquid. If the rice looks dry but is still hard, add 2–3 tbsp hot water and continue baking.
Let the dish rest for about 5 minutes before serving.

name: Proja
ingredients:
For 1 small baking dish:
2 eggs
200 g yogurt or skyr
150 g cornmeal
100 g čajna salama, chopped into small pieces
1 tsp baking powder
Pinch of salt
Optional: 50–100 g grated or crumbled cheese
A little oil or butter for greasing the baking dish
instructions:
Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk until combined. Add the yogurt or skyr and mix until smooth.
Add the cornmeal, baking powder and a pinch of salt. Stir until everything is evenly combined and you have a thick batter.
Cut the čajna salama into small pieces and fold it into the mixture. If using cheese, add it now and mix again.
Lightly grease a small baking dish with oil or butter. Pour in the batter and spread it evenly.
Bake at 190°C for 25–35 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the centre feels firm. A knife or toothpick inserted into the middle should come out mostly clean.
Let the proja rest for 5–10 minutes before cutting and serving.

name: Vegeta Chicken Steak
ingredients:
For 1 portion:
1 chicken breast or chicken steak
1–2 tsp Vegeta seasoning
1 tsp oil
Optional: 1 small piece of butter
instructions:
Pat the chicken dry with a paper towel. If the chicken breast is very thick, gently flatten it or cut it into a thinner steak so it cooks evenly.
Season both sides generously with Vegeta. You usually do not need extra salt because Vegeta is already salty.
Heat a pan over medium to medium-high heat. Add 1 tsp oil and let it heat for a few seconds.
Place the chicken in the pan and leave it undisturbed for about 4–6 minutes on the first side, depending on its thickness.
Flip the chicken and cook for another 4–6 minutes. Lower the heat slightly if the outside is browning too quickly.
Optional: add a small piece of butter during the last 1–2 minutes and spoon the melted butter over the chicken.
Remove from the pan when the centre is fully cooked and no longer pink. Let it rest for 3–5 minutes before cutting so it stays juicy.

name: Pan-Fried Salmon
ingredients:
For 1 portion:
½ of a 300 g salmon piece (150 g salmon)
Salt
Pepper
Paprika
Garlic powder
1 tbsp butter
instructions:
Pat the 150 g salmon piece dry. Season both sides with salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder.
Heat a pan on 4/6 for about 1 minute. Your stove runs hot, so 4/6 is usually enough. Add 1 tbsp butter and let it melt.
Place the salmon in the pan. Cook the first side for about 3–4 minutes without moving it too much so it develops a nice crust.
Flip the salmon and lower the heat slightly to around 3–4/6. Cover the pan with a lid and cook the second side for another 3–4 minutes.
If the salmon piece is especially thick, keep it covered on low heat for another 1–2 minutes. It should flake easily with a fork when done.

name: Creamy Garlic Shrimp Pasta
ingredients:
For 1 portion:
100–120 g pasta
150 g shrimp, peeled
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp butter
1 tsp oil
1 tbsp flour
200 ml milk
Salt
Pepper
Paprika
Optional: 20–30 g grated parmesan
Optional: parsley, chilli flakes or lemon juice
No fresh garlic? Use about 1 tsp garlic powder instead. Add it with the flour so it doesn't burn.
instructions:
Cook the pasta in salted water according to the package instructions. Before draining, save about ¼ cup (60 ml) of the pasta water.
Season the shrimp with salt, pepper and paprika. Heat a pan on about 4/6 and melt the butter with the oil. Add the minced garlic and cook for 30–45 seconds until fragrant but not brown. If using garlic powder, wait and add it with the flour.
Add the shrimp and cook for about 1½–2 minutes per side, until pink and just cooked through. Remove the shrimp from the pan and set them aside so they don't overcook.
Lower the heat to about 2–3/6. Sprinkle in the flour and stir continuously for about 1 minute to cook out the raw flour taste.
Slowly pour in the milk while whisking or stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the sauce thickens. If it becomes too thick, add a splash of the reserved pasta water.
Return the shrimp to the pan. Add the cooked pasta and toss everything together until coated in the sauce. If using parmesan, stir it in now until melted. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Finish with parsley, chilli flakes or a squeeze of lemon juice if desired.

name: TikTok Noodles
ingredients:
For 1 portion:
1 packet instant noodles
1 tbsp butter
1–2 garlic cloves, minced OR ½–1 tsp garlic powder
1 tsp brown sugar
1 tsp sesame seeds
1 noodle seasoning packet
Optional: spring onion, chilli flakes or a fried egg

No brown sugar? Use about ¾ tsp honey instead. Since honey can burn more easily, add it together with the seasoning after lowering the heat.
instructions:
Cook the noodles according to the package instructions, but drain them about 30 seconds before they are completely done. Save 2–3 tbsp of the noodle water before draining.
Heat a pan on low-medium heat, about 3/6, and melt 1 tbsp butter. Add the minced garlic and cook for only 30–45 seconds, until fragrant but not brown. If using garlic powder instead, don't add it directly to the butter yet because it can burn easily.
Lower the heat to about 2/6. Add 1 tsp brown sugar, 1 tsp sesame seeds and the noodle seasoning packet. If using garlic powder, add it now. Add 1–2 tbsp noodle water and stir for about 20–30 seconds until everything dissolves into a glossy sauce.
Add the cooked noodles and toss everything together for 1–2 minutes until the noodles are evenly coated and have absorbed most of the sauce. Add another splash of noodle water if they look too dry.
Taste before adding any extra salt because the seasoning packet is already salty. Finish with extra sesame seeds, spring onion or chilli flakes if desired.
